title: Rigging faces generated by Meshy or Tripo
author: Chaibi_Alaa
selftext:
Hello everyone,

I am working on an arcade/combat game like MK or Street Fighter and that kind of games, and after generating some really beautiful characters on Meshy and Tripo I'm having a real hard time rigging the face (eyes, mouth) for dialogues specifically. I tried some open source models in RunPod, Claude Opus, Codex, no chance. I started testing with Fable and the image attached showcases the latest level I reached. 

Do you have any clue to how to resolve this ? 

  
Thanks !

comments.author: cxfoulke
comments.body:
Good Luck everything ive experienced with meshy has been pretty garbage. The vertices count of models is through the roof.  they are no way built like a proper model for animation.  

They have probably improved the topology since the last time i tried it but i doubt it works well.  

Never mind things like it seperating hair or clothes from the base model. 

Honestly if you want my take give up on anything "realistic"  try some very simple models. Claude and co can mcp in blender or programatically build some janky models. 

Build the game get everything down to perfection narrative, flow, feeling.  If you get there maybe ai modeling is better by then or maybe you really feel like the game has a chance and then you can invest it. Or set off some code tasks and watch a bunch of blender tutorials haha

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
You're not going to be able to rig generated model faces for proper deformation. That's an area you're going to have to manually remesh to have a chance. It can look at an arm on a body and go, "This mesh shouldn't be fused to the main body." It can't look at a face and go, "This mouth needs to be able to open and close." At least not yet.

If your game is more stylized, your best bet is to not fuck around with the topo of the face at all, and instead create a number of expressions you swap between that are painted onto the face. Just key the expressions to different parts of the UV and swap like you would for expressions in a 2d spritesheet based game.

comments.author: lordpoee
comments.body: Yeah....AI 3D generated models still have a way to go. I had some success by instructing the AI to generate models as component parts rather than solid meshes, for sure though, you need to spend some time in blender un-forking these models. Many times they have way too many polys and you'll have to cut and clip and get your rig set manually.
